To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a computational model of generalization of face perception from a single view to novel views and expressions can be constructed, and it performs at a level comparable to human observers.

(1) the model generalizes from a single view to a range of views and to additional expressions with a performance that is close to human performance in the same task and that (2) the model generalization performance is sensitive to the number of familiar views, the range of views, and the number of expressions.

a computational model can learn a face representation that generalizes to novel views and expressions, that the model can be used for recognition of novel faces, and that it performs well compared with human subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational theory of human face recognition.
the generalization of recognition over viewing conditions.
the generalization problem in face recognition, and the model proposed here is the first computational model of generalization from a novel view to a range of views and expressions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model generalizes from a single view to a range of poses and expressions, and that it is comparable to the human observer in the one out /spl sim/ three discrimination task.
the model is not a good model of human face recognition, but that it is a reasonable model of the generalization process in the face of changes in viewing conditions and facial expressions.
the model is not yet as good as human observers, but is a promising first step toward the goal of a general model of human face recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a computational model for generalization of human face recognition that is capable of generalization over viewpoint and expression.
a model that is capable of generalizing from one view to a range of poses and expressions can be constructed, and that it performs well in comparison to human observers.
a model of face recognition can be built on a single view/exposition to the extent that the model is capable of generalizing over pose and expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generalization of faces from one view/expression to others may be achieved through a combination of similarity-based interpolation and a small set of face transformations.
generalization over pose and expression is possible with only a single view of the face.
a single view is sufficient to generalize face identity over a wide range of poses and expressions.
